latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The image passed the presence, count, and attribute checks for two spotted chairs, striped bicycles, and one red trumpet, and it passed the relation that the bicycles are behind the trumpet. It failed the spatial relation requiring the chairs to be on top of the bicycles, the exact count of two bicycles was not strong enough, and the trumpet presence score was weak despite the one-red-trumpet count and color checks passing. The next prompt should make the two bicycles fully separate and countable, make the red trumpet large and unmistakable in the foreground, and use a more concrete stacked layout where each spotted chair is visibly resting directly on the top of a striped bicycle.
expected_improvement: The chairs-on-top-of-bicycles relation should improve by explicitly placing each spotted chair directly on the seat/top frame area of a bicycle, above the wheels.
The bicycle count should improve by showing exactly two separate striped bicycles side by side with both wheels visible on each bicycle and no extra bicycles.
The trumpet presence should improve by making the single red trumpet prominent, complete, and unobstructed in the foreground while keeping the bicycles behind it.
preserve_constraints: Keep both chairs spotted, with the spotted pattern bound only to the chairs.
Keep chairs present and not cropped out.
Keep bicycles present and striped, with the striped pattern bound only to the bicycles.
Keep the two striped bicycles behind the red trumpet.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt stated that chairs should be on top of bicycles, but did not make the support contact visually concrete enough, so the generator likely produced chairs near or above bicycles rather than clearly resting on them. It also allowed the foreground trumpet to potentially reduce bicycle count clarity or trumpet recognizability.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Insufficiently explicit spatial_layout, quantity_counting, and clarity_visibility instructions for a difficult stacked multi-object composition.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple staged composition: one foreground red trumpet, and behind it exactly two separate striped bicycles placed side by side. Put one spotted chair directly on top of each bicycle, visibly resting on the bicycle seat/top frame area above the wheels. Keep all objects complete, separated enough to count, and avoid extra duplicates.
regression_risks: The red trumpet in the foreground could occlude the bicycles too much and make the two-bicycle count fail.
The generator could add extra bicycle-like wheels or partial bicycles when trying to show two bicycles.
The generator could show chairs beside the bicycles instead of physically on top of them.
The spotted and striped attributes could leak to the wrong objects if not bound explicitly.
repair_constraints: Show exactly two striped bicycles, no more and no less, as two distinct complete bicycles with visible frames and wheels.
Place the two spotted chairs on top of the two striped bicycles: each chair must sit directly above and in contact with a bicycle seat/top frame, clearly higher than the bicycle wheels.
Show exactly one red trumpet prominently in the foreground, complete and easy to recognize.
Keep both striped bicycles behind the single red trumpet while still visible and countable.
Do not add extra chairs, bicycles, trumpets, wheels, or duplicate instruments.

Place the single red trumpet large and unmistakable in the foreground in front of the bicycles, but do not let it hide the two bicycles. Keep the attributes bound correctly: only the two chairs are spotted, only the two bicycles are striped, and the one trumpet is red. No extra chairs, no extra bicycles, no extra trumpets, no duplicate wheels or partial extra bicycles; all required objects are fully visible and easy to count.
